newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria, Russia draft gas transit agreement.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, Russia draft gas transit agreement.

text.p: Bulgaria and Russia on Tuesday agreed the terms of a long-delayed intergovernmental pact on transiting Russian natural gas via Bulgaria, an official statement said.
A Bulgarian government statement said the agreement would be signed by interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin in Moscow in the coming days.
Bulgaria will build the pipelines on its territory and will pay for them through transit fees. The statement gave no financial details.

"The agreement is based on the principle that the newly built gas pipelines for transiting Russian natural gas will be fully paid for by part of the fees (collected) from the increased volumes of transiting gas," the statement said.
"Thus the Bulgarian side will not be burdened with financial outlays for the construction of the new capacity."
Senior officials from Russia's Gazprom , headed by vice-president Bogdan Bodzulyak, arrived in Sofia on Monday.

Bulgaria has a gas network of some 2,000 km. An enlargement of the network will be needed as gas supplies to Turkey will be increased and the project envisages gas supplies to Greece, Macedonia, Serbia and possibly Albania in the future.
Gazprom has assigned a Bulgarian-Russian stock company Topenergy to finance and participate in the construction of the new pipelines, the statement said.

Topenergy was set up last year by Gazprom, which has a 50 percent share, and Bulgaria's state-owned gas distributor Bulgargas, which holds a 25.1 percent stake. The remaining 24.9 percent are distributed among Bulgarian banks and firms.
Bulgaria will pay for part of its gas supplies in Bulgarian goods and services in Russia, the statement said.
The two sides have recently registered in Moscow a joint venture, which will settle part of Bulgaria's payments by barter, Bulgargas executive director Vasil Filipov said.

Sofia and Moscow will share the stakes in the venture, named ZAO Inter Trans Investitsii i Torgovli (ITIT), he said. Bulgargas and Russia's Inter Investmarket hold 40 percent each in ITIT and Bulgaria's Biochim Bank and Russia's AKB Stolichnii Bank Sberejenie hold a 10 percent stake each.

Bulgaria, which lacks energy resources and imports gas only from Russia, needs some six billion cubic metres of natural gas per year, Filipov said. The private firm Overgas, which is half-owned by Gazprom, will deliver the gas supplies to Bulgaria, he added.

The terms for building the new pipelines and the prices of gas supplies and transiting fees will be fixed in commercial contracts between Bulgargas and suppliers selected by Gazprom, the statement said.
